evals.prompt: I have a draft LunaTalk role card with a clear premise and decent first scene. Before creating or publishing anything, give me a top-tier quality scorecard and the first three repairs.
evals.expected_output: Produces a quality audit packet with evidence-backed 0-4 scores, overall tier, blockers, strongest and weakest dimensions, first three repairs, skill handoff order, and no MCP calls.
expectations: The output uses lunatalk-quality-auditor rather than publish readiness, simulation, or broad authoring.
The scorecard covers promise, archetype, engine, agency, opening, second-turn, longplay, voice, boundary, token, presentation, and testability as applicable.
The audit flags blockers before assigning an overall tier.
The first three repairs are concrete and map to Moonloom skills or fields.
The output treats scores as craft guidance, not platform metrics or MCP validation.

evals.prompt: Score this companion blueprint before I make it real. It has strong chemistry but I am not sure if it has enough player agency, longplay, and refusal behavior.
evals.expected_output: Reviews the blueprint as a craft audit, marks irrelevant dimensions as N/A, scores agency/longplay/boundary carefully, and recommends targeted next skills before card-author.
expectations: The output does not call mutating MCP tools for a blueprint audit.
The scorecard uses N/A for dimensions that do not apply instead of forcing every card into every archetype.
The audit checks player agency, longplay, and boundary handling before recommending authoring.
The repairs route to agency, longplay, or boundary skills when those dimensions are weak.
The output keeps the audit public-safe and original.

evals.prompt: This draft looks polished and the XMLV3 is pretty, but I want to know if it is actually a strong card or just a nice first screen. Audit it without simulating.
evals.expected_output: Separates presentation quality from playability, scores durable engine, agency, second turn, longplay, token allocation, and recommends structural repairs before render or simulation.
expectations: The output says readable or pretty presentation is not proof of playability.
The audit scores presentation separately from durable engine, agency, second-turn, and longplay.
The first repairs do not focus only on CSS, Theme V3, or visual polish.
The output delays simulation when structural repairs are already evident.
The output does not turn the scorecard into an MCP/server gate.

evals.prompt: Audit a quiet daily-life blueprint before authoring. The mood is gentle and pretty, but I worry it has no small desire, no habit state, no return-next-time hook, and no way for a passive player to matter.
evals.expected_output: Scores daily-life engine quality as craft guidance, flags missing routine/state/renewal blockers, and recommends lunatalk-daily-life-architect before authoring or simulation.
expectations: The audit scores daily-life engine separately from presentation and general relationship tone.
The blockers include missing small desire, habit state, player leverage, passive-player behavior, or return-next-time hook as applicable.
The first repairs route to lunatalk-daily-life-architect or daily-life-design before card-author.
The scorecard remains public craft guidance and not platform metrics, analytics, or MCP validation.
The output does not call mutating MCP tools.

evals.prompt: Audit this coherent packet stack before field assembly. The engine, opening, and longplay are strong, but the promise score is weak because roleName is generic, roleDesc is too long, tags are vague, and the first impression does not explain why to open it. Do not call MCP tools.
evals.expected_output: Uses lunatalk-quality-auditor for the scorecard, marks profile packaging as the first promise repair, and hands off to lunatalk-profile-packager without MCP calls.
expectations: The output keeps the task in lunatalk-quality-auditor because the user asked for an audit or scorecard.
The promise dimension identifies weak roleName, roleDesc, tags, and first-impression reason-to-open as the main weak layer.
The first repair or handoff routes to lunatalk-profile-packager before card-author, render, simulation, or publish readiness.
The output preserves the coherent engine, opening, and longplay instead of broad diagnosis or re-blueprinting.
The output does not call MCP tools or treat profile quality as platform metrics or an MCP gate.

evals.prompt: Audit this coherent zh-Hant packet stack before field assembly. Character core, opening, longplay, and voice are strong, but profile/detail/welcome/examples mix Simplified and Traditional Chinese, pronouns drift, tags are partly English, and talkExample uses a different register from detail. Do not call MCP tools.
evals.expected_output: Uses lunatalk-quality-auditor for the scorecard, marks language style as a narrow weak layer, and hands off to lunatalk-language-stylist without MCP calls.
expectations: The output keeps the task in lunatalk-quality-auditor because the user asked for an audit or scorecard.
The language-style dimension identifies script mixing, pronoun drift, mixed tags, and register mismatch as the main weak layer.
The first repair or handoff routes to lunatalk-language-stylist before card-author, render, simulation, or publish readiness.
The output preserves the coherent engine, opening, longplay, and voice instead of broad diagnosis or re-blueprinting.
The output does not call MCP tools or treat language style as platform metrics or an MCP gate.
